implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's proofs over the issue-volume harness (Postgres 17 + pgvector on 127.0.0.1:25433, nats-server on 24222) at the head's code commit 6720ccae. The go-package proofs (A3/A4/A5/A6/A9 in internal/workflow, internal/daemon scratch-dispatch, internal/store, internal/supervise) reproduce green in a full `go test ./...`. But the A13/R11 proof is false at the head: its own command `bun test packages/pi-legion/` reports 4 failures, not '91 pass, 0 fail', and the failing tests are the very read_state ones the proof cites. failures.criterion: A1 (a test in the package the change touches passes at the change) / A13,R11 (read_state summary under 30 KB with every key; filters return full records) — packages/pi-legion is RED at the head.
failures.evidence: cd /legion/workspaces/sjawhar/legion/infra-714 && bun install && bun test packages/pi-legion/src/tools.test.ts → 9 pass, 4 fail (deterministic, re-run after bun install): (fail) 'read_state with no field summarizes 92 issues under the tool's limit, naming every one'; (fail) "read_state's filters answer full records, and name what they cannot select"; (fail) 'the legion tool's parameter schema serializes to the exact schema Oh My Pi agents are given, for every session'; (fail) 'the controller reads the state without a grant and sets an issue's status with its own'. All four raise the same ZodError parsing the test's state fixture: `repositories.withoutWebhookApp` 'expected array, received undefined' and `consumers` 'expected array, received undefined'. Root cause: the contracts LegionState schema requires both (packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts:465 withoutWebhookApp, :511 consumers; contract 43, brought in by the #2478 forward merge) but the state fixture at packages/pi-legion/src/tools.test.ts:943 builds `repositories: { owners, mapped, refused, caches }` with no withoutWebhookApp and no top-level consumers. The forward merge was not reconciled with the pi-legion fixtures. Fix: add the two arrays to the test's state fixture (one shared fixture; one edit clears all four). Source-level and environment-independent, so CI's bun test / pi-legion job is red at this head.

failures.criterion: A1 / R1,R5 — internal/admit TestReadmissionStartsTheNewGenerationWithoutTheOldGenerationsFacts passes on main 8a911ecca3a5 and fails at the head.
failures.evidence: At the head: cd packages/daemon && eval "$(bash $TMPDIR/harness/up.sh)" && go test ./internal/admit/ -run TestReadmissionStartsTheNewGenerationWithoutTheOldGenerationsFacts -count=1 → FAIL: `admit_test.go:738: gen2-approved = intake.Result{Refusal:(*intake.Refusal)(nil), Duplicate:false}, claim token: "LEGION-LINGER" is not an issue key`. Same command in /legion/scratch/tmp/main714 (main 8a911ecca3a5) → ok (PASS). Root cause: the new gate-message path workflow.(*Engine).tellGateMoved (packages/daemon/internal/workflow/gate.go:730 and :751-754) builds a claim.NewToken for the tree architect and each phase holder and `return err` on failure, which aborts the whole applyArtifact/ApplyFact transaction for the gate-open (DispatchArtifactApproved) fact. The readmission fixture's key `LEGION-LINGER` has no numeric suffix, so claim.NewToken (claim/token.go:55-58, issueKey regexp) errors. Real Dispatch keys are PROJECT-<number> so this never fires in production, but the branch turns an existing green test red (CI's daemon test job goes red), and a messaging-token error aborting a critical gate-open transition is fragile. Fix is the implementer's call: a valid-key fixture, or make tellGateMoved tolerant of a per-member token-build failure. Deterministic in isolation.

Fix: update that assertion to match the intended approved-head-free merger task. Deterministic.
